thread:
Marta (Eng): Quick question for People Ops 50% chance this is dumb50. I have 12 hours of carryover left but I heard there's a cap on how much carryover can be applied against blackout days. If I file for Dec 22-23, will carryover be used or rejected?

PeopleOps Bot: FYI: annual carryover cap is governed by PTO policy 4.1. Time off during blackout (Dec 20-27) still requires manager + People Ops sign-off. See People Ops for exception rules.

Marta (Eng): Cool. Only reason I'm asking is I want to WFH on the 23rd and thought we sometimes allow remote work instead of taking PTO in the blackout. Is that a thing?

Jon (People Ops): Short answer: No automatic WFH substitution for blackout days. If you plan to work remotely during the holiday window, that is fine but you must still request time off for the portion you will be unavailable. Substitutions (work in lieu of PTO) are handled case-by-case and require manager attestation plus People Ops approval.

Ken (Manager): Marta, what's the ask? Full day off both days or partial? If partial, we can try to shift meetings and have you do asynchronous coverage.

Marta (Eng): Prefer full day on 22 and afternoon 23. I have 12h carryover and about 8h current-year accrual. That should cover it unless there's a cap preventing use of carryover in blackout.

PeopleOps Bot: Reminder: carryover cap is 40 hours max carried into the new year; usage during blackout is allowed but subject to exception rules if the role is coverage-critical.

Jon (People Ops): We allow carryover to be consumed during blackout requests. The only limitation is if an exception is being requested to exceed the normal blackout allowances (e.g., granting PTO without sufficient accrual) we may require unpaid marking. If you have enough accrual + carryover, it should be fine. Submit the request and tag me; I can pre-check balances.

Irene (Payroll): For clarity on accounting: if carryover is used in December, it reduces your carryover pool for year-end and is reflected in the W-2 accrual reconciliation. No special tax implication, but managers should avoid approving carryover-heavy requests that would leave teams under-rostered.

Luca (IC): Quick anecdote 50 last year I had to use carryover on blackout and People Ops approved after we showed who covered my pager. Cover plan matters.

Ken (Manager): I'll coordinate a coverage plan. Marta, can you push the critical deploy to Dec 21 or hand off to Luca?

Marta (Eng): Yep I can move the deploy to the 21st. Filing request now.

Marta (Eng): Submitted TimeOff ID 20321004 as "Blackout Exception - use accrual + carryover". Attached manager attestation and coverage plan.

Jon (People Ops): Got it. I'll review balances and confirm. If anything short, we'll mark unpaid for the delta. Expect response within 48 hours.

PeopleOps Bot: Request 20321004 queued for review.

Jon (People Ops): Approved. Marked as "Blackout Exception Approved: accrual+carryover used, coverage verified". Policy refs PTO-3.2 and PTO-4.1. Audit note EX-2026-19.

Marta (Eng): Thank you! I'll update calendar and handover notes.

Irene (Payroll): Noted in payroll feed. Carryover usage reduced by 12 hours.

Marta (Eng): Appreciate the quick turnaround :sparkles:
